class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Add a CI job to this repository that runs Muse Code headless on demand: install the CLI, confirm `muse --version`, and run `muse exec` with META_API_KEY taken from the CI secret store (a secret named MUSE_KEY), --disable-approval, a --max-model-steps cap and --contributor-mode off. Then run the project&#x27;s own tests as the real gate. Use the CI system this repo already has, or GitHub Actions if it has none.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Authentication and billing&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/auth.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/auth

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Muse Code reads META_API_KEY. An API key always beats a browser sign-in: META_API_KEY, then a key stored with `muse auth set`, then a stored browser session.
- CI has no browser: pass the secret through the environment, as in `META_API_KEY=&quot;$MUSE_KEY&quot; muse exec &quot;...&quot;`. Never echo it or write it to a file.
- Meta Managed Accounts (Business &amp; Enterprise sign-up) can&#x27;t use the browser sign-in; they always use an API key.
- `muse logout` clears the stored session and stored key, never an exported META_API_KEY.
- Headless runs can&#x27;t answer approval prompts: --disable-approval keeps the sandbox; --yolo drops it and trusts the workspace, so only in a disposable container with trusted code.
- Pin Contributor mode per run (`--contributor-mode off` or MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE=0): saved settings differ by machine.

Starter code (Python)
import os
import subprocess
import sys

# CI step: META_API_KEY comes from the pipeline&#x27;s secret store, never from the repo.
if not os.environ.get(&quot;META_API_KEY&quot;):
    sys.exit(&quot;META_API_KEY isn&#x27;t set: add it from your CI secret store.&quot;)

cmd = [&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, &quot;--disable-approval&quot;, &quot;--max-model-steps&quot;, &quot;40&quot;,
       &quot;--contributor-mode&quot;, &quot;off&quot;, &quot;Run the test suite and summarize failures.&quot;]
run = subprocess.run(cmd, text=True)
if run.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(f&quot;muse exec ended with exit code {run.returncode}&quot;)
# Exit 0 means the turn completed, not that the work is right: gate on the tests.
subprocess.run([&quot;npm&quot;, &quot;test&quot;], check=True)

Done when
- The job uses the secret only through the environment (secrets.MUSE_KEY or $MUSE_KEY); no key appears anywhere in the repo.
- A manual run installs muse, prints its version, runs the prompt, then runs the tests and fails the job when they fail.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,079<!-- --> Remove that from your shell or secret store separately.</p><h2 id="billing" class="docs-h docs-h2">Billing and plans<a class="docs-anchor" href="#billing" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><h3 id="billing-setup" class="docs-h docs-h3">Billing setup<a class="docs-anchor" href="#billing-setup" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">Meta Model API billing is usage-based: you&#x27;re billed for the tokens your requests consume. This page explains how to set up billing and how charges work. For step-by-step instructions, see how to <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/help/billing/set-up-billing" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">set up billing<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> and <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/help/billing/download-invoice" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">download invoices<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> in the Help Center.</p><p class="docs-p">Prefer a flat monthly rate instead of pay-as-you-go pricing? See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/subscriptions">subscriptions</a>.</p><h3 id="add-payment" class="docs-h docs-h3">How to add payment<a class="docs-anchor" href="#add-payment" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">A team admin needs to complete two steps:</p><ol class="docs-list" start="1"><li><span><strong>Add a payment method.</strong> Go to <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/billing" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Billing<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> and add a payment method. See <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/help/billing/set-up-billing" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">How to set up billing<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> for detailed instructions.</span></li><li><span><strong>Create an API key.</strong> See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/authentication">Authentication</a> for instructions.</span></li></ol><p class="docs-p">Only team admins can manage payment methods and business information.</p><h3 id="how-billing-works" class="docs-h docs-h3">How billing works<a class="docs-anchor" href="#how-billing-works" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">Charges are based on token usage. Every request consumes:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Input tokens</strong>: your prompt, system instructions, and conversation history.</span></li><li><span><strong>Output tokens</strong>: the text the model generates. Output tokens typically cost more than input tokens.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Costs may vary by model. For current per-model rates, see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/pricing-rate-limits">Pricing and rate limits</a>.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">What counts as a token</p><p class="docs-p">A token is roughly 3–4 characters of English text. Non-English text and code often use more tokens per word, so equivalent requests can cost more depending on the language and content type. Use the <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/usage" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Usage dashboard<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> to see how many tokens your requests consume.</p></div></div><h3 id="when-charged" class="docs-h docs-h3">When you&#x27;re charged<a class="docs-anchor" href="#when-charged" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">Charges accrue as you use the API. Your payment method is charged in one of two situations:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Payment threshold reached.</strong> Whenever your current balance reaches your payment threshold amount, your payment method is charged for that amount. As you make successful payments, your payment threshold may be raised until your account reaches a final threshold amount.</span></li><li><span><strong>Monthly bill date.</strong> Any remaining balance is automatically charged on the first of each month.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">If you have a current balance, you can use <strong>Pay now</strong> on the <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/billing" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Billing<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> page to make an early payment before you reach your payment threshold or monthly bill date.</p><h2 id="next-steps" class="docs-h docs-h2">Next steps<a class="docs-anchor" href="#next-steps" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><ul repository.

Task
Add a CI job to this repository that runs Muse Code headless on demand: install the CLI, confirm `muse --version`, and run `muse exec` with META_API_KEY taken from the CI secret store (a secret named MUSE_KEY), --disable-approval, a --max-model-steps cap and --contributor-mode off. Then run the project&#x27;s own tests as the real gate. Use the CI system this repo already has, or GitHub Actions if it has none.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Authentication and billing&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/auth.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/auth

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Muse Code reads META_API_KEY. An API key always beats a browser sign-in: META_API_KEY, then a key stored with `muse auth set`, then a stored browser session.
- CI has no browser: pass the secret through the environment, as in `META_API_KEY=&quot;$MUSE_KEY&quot; muse exec &quot;...&quot;`. Never echo it or write it to a file.
- Meta Managed Accounts (Business &amp; Enterprise sign-up) can&#x27;t use the browser sign-in; they always use an API key.
- `muse logout` clears the stored session and stored key, never an exported META_API_KEY.
- Headless runs can&#x27;t answer approval prompts: --disable-approval keeps the sandbox; --yolo drops it and trusts the workspace, so only in a disposable container with trusted code.
- Pin Contributor mode per run (`--contributor-mode off` or MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE=0): saved settings differ by machine.

Starter code (Python)
import os
import subprocess
import sys

# CI step: META_API_KEY comes from the pipeline&#x27;s secret store, never from the repo.
if not os.environ.get(&quot;META_API_KEY&quot;):
    sys.exit(&quot;META_API_KEY isn&#x27;t set: add it from your CI secret store.&quot;)

cmd = [&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, &quot;--disable-approval&quot;, &quot;--max-model-steps&quot;, &quot;40&quot;,
       &quot;--contributor-mode&quot;, &quot;off&quot;, &quot;Run the test suite and summarize failures.&quot;]
run = subprocess.run(cmd, text=True)
if run.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(f&quot;muse exec ended with exit code {run.returncode}&quot;)
# Exit 0 means the turn completed, not that the work is right: gate on the tests.
subprocess.run([&quot;npm&quot;, &quot;test&quot;], check=True)

Done when
- The job uses the secret only through the environment (secrets.MUSE_KEY or $MUSE_KEY); no key appears anywhere in the repo.
- A manual run installs muse, prints its version, runs the prompt, then runs the tests and fails the job when they fail.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,079<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/auth" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
